questions.question: Before a trip, you should make sure that:

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The pedal grooves are not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal grooves are not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Before your trip, check that nothing blocks your pedals. Make sure the brake and gas pedals work properly. The pedal surfaces should have grooves to prevent your foot from slipping.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you will receive points if you:

options.text: Pull up once.
Check your positioning.
Cross over exercise boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross over exercise boundaries.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each crossing counts as an error and lowers your test score.

questions.question: During the driving test, when encountering a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: If your bus has a manual transmission, what should you never do when crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Change gears.
Use the brakes.
Look both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Your vehicle could stall and become stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: Active railroad crossings:

options.text: Have traffic control devices installed.
Do not have any traffic control devices installed.
Are crossed by at least 10 vehicles every hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have traffic control devices installed.
questions.explanation: Active railroad crossings have control devices such as flashing red lights, warning bells, or gates. These devices control traffic at the crossing. By law, you must follow these control devices.

questions.question: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors allow you to see all of the following, except:

options.text: The right and left front tires touching the ground.
The area in front of the bus.
The tops of the right and left rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tops of the right and left rear tires.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors show the area in front of the bus from ground level, the right and left front tires touching the ground, and the area from the front of the bus to the service door. They do not show the tops of the rear tires.

questions.question: When performing a pre-trip inspection and looking into the fifth wheel gap, you should:

options.text: Make sure the locking jaws are open.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When checking the trailer coupling, make sure the fifth wheel locking jaws are completely closed around the kingpin shank. The jaws must not be open or loose.

questions.question: When a school bus is approaching a bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Not use the mirrors.
Approach with caution.
Drive quickly and stop abruptly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach with caution.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers must approach stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: A bus driver approaching a bus stop should stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students because:

options.text: The students will have to walk to the bus, allowing you to see their movements.
Buses are difficult to drive.
The students may get scared of the bus coming toward them.

questions.correctAnswerText: The students will have to walk to the bus, allowing you to see their movements.
questions.explanation: Stop your bus with the front bumper at least 10 feet from waiting students. This makes students walk toward the bus, so you can watch their movements.

questions.question: The overhead rearview mirror is located:

options.text: On the right side of a bus.
On the steering wheel of a bus.
Above the windshield inside a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside a bus.
questions.explanation: On a school bus, the overhead rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield inside the bus on the driver's side. Use this mirror to watch students inside the bus.

questions.question: If there is a fire on a school bus, the students:

options.text: Must leave the bus.
Should stay on the bus but move to an area away from the fire.
Should stay in their seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must leave the bus.
questions.explanation: If a school bus catches fire or there is a fire threat, the bus driver must get all students off the bus right away.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections should be done:

options.text: Differently each time to check different items.
The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
Once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do the same pre-trip inspection before every drive. This helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you don't skip anything.

questions.question: When doing an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay inside the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: During the driving test, when asked to change lanes:

options.text: You don't need to worry about other drivers.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes quickly, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes during the driving test, check your mirrors, use your turn signal, and change lanes smoothly when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When students board a bus, they should:

options.text: Sit in the back row first.
Use the back row only after all other seats are full.
Sit as far from the driver as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the back row only after all other seats are full.
questions.explanation: Students should not sit in the back row unless the bus is full. Sitting closer to the front is safer if the bus is hit from behind. Students with special needs should sit near the driver.

questions.question: Bus doors should be closed while driving, except when:

options.text: Crossing railroad tracks.
You need to cool off the bus.
There is no vehicle next to the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Keep bus doors closed whenever the bus is moving, except when crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: School buses:

options.text: Never have ABS.
Only have ABS in cold climates.
May have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have ABS.
questions.explanation: Most commercial vehicles made after 1998 or 1999 must have anti-lock brakes (ABS). Many older buses also have ABS.

questions.question: The overhead rearview mirror is located:

options.text: On the outside left of the bus.
On the outside right of the bus.
Above the windshield inside the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside the bus.
questions.explanation: In a school bus, the overhead rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side.

questions.question: If your bus stalls on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Get everyone off the bus and move far away from it.
Keep everyone on the bus and try to wave down the train to stop it.
Keep everyone on the bus and wait for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get everyone off the bus and move far away from it.
questions.explanation: If the bus stalls on railroad tracks, get everyone off the bus immediately and move away from the tracks. Move at an angle away from the tracks in the direction of any oncoming train.

questions.question: When doing a conventional parallel parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Back up past the parking space, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For conventional parallel parking into a space on your right, drive past the space first, then back into it. Bring the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must stay inside the space boundaries.
